newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario's Eves to give fiscal update on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Ontario's Eves to give fiscal update on Thursday.

text.p: Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves will present a mid-year fiscal and economic update on Thursday, the provincial finance ministry said on Wednesday.
Eves was scheduled to speak to the Ontario legislature's standing committee on finance and economic affairs at 1530 EST/2030 GMT, the ministry said in a statement.

Finance officials said the update would not include details of further spending cuts planned by the Conservative government. "What everybody is expecting as far as what the government is going to do is going to be held off for a little while," said spokeswoman Karin Dillabough.
The Conservatives swept to power in June, 1995 and promised to wipe out a C$8.7 billion budget deficit by 2000-01.
About C$6 billion in cuts have been outlined so far. The upcoming mini-budget is expected to detail where the remaining C$3 billion will be cut.
Dillabough said one reason for the delay is that a review of government operations has not been completed. The mini-budget may not come until after Christmas, she said.
